sentences.text: the Tribunal.

2. By the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.8,86,000/- to the appellants/claimants on account of death of deceased- Duruj Nayak, husband of appellant-1,
father of appellants-2, 3, 4, and 5, and son of appellant-6,

who died in motor accident that took place on 04.10.2017 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, Pick-up vehicle bearing registration No.CG-04 ZD- 5560, driven by respondent-1 Rakesh Goyal, owned by respondent-2 Chaman Nishad, and insured by the Oriental Insurance Company, respondent-3.
3.

As per the pleadings, the deceased-Duruj Nayak was running a grocery shop at the village-Dewanpali, and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, and the appellants/claimants are dependents on the income of the deceased.

4. Respondents-1 and 2, driver and owner of the offending vehicle have proceeded ex parte, and not contested the claim of the appellants.
5. Respondent-3 Insurance Company denied the claim of the claimants before the Claims Tribunal,
and submitted that at the time of accident, Driver of the offending vehicle was not having any valid and effective driving license with him, and the vehicle was being driven without fitness and permit,
thereby, there is breach of Policy conditions, and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

On the basis of above pleadings, learned Claims Tribunal has framed six issues and after appreciating the oral as well as documentary evidence available on record, decided the same in favour of the appellants/claimants, and the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month as Notional Income and awarded the above stated amount towards compensation.
7.

Shri Ravi Kumar Kashyap, learned counsel for the appellants would submit that the deceased was aged about 28 years on the date of accident and was running a grocery shop in the village- Dewanpali, by which he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, and his income should have been considered accordingly.

In alternative, he would submit that looking to the age and occupation of the deceased, atleast minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident should have been taken into consideration for assessment of the compensation amount.
The amount awarded towards other heads is also on lower side and therefore, amount of compensation is liable to be enhanced suitably.

8. On the other hand, Shri HS Patel, learned counsel for the Insurance Company would support the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal, and would submit that looking to the age, and occupation of the deceased, the Tribunal has rightly considered the claim of the claimants.

The claimants have not produced any document to prove that the deceased was running a grocery shop and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, and therefore, the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is fully justified, which needs no interference by this court.
Smt. Jharna Nayak vs Rakesh Goyal on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16865311/
2 Mac 62 of 2021 9.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10. Barring the oral evidence of the appellants/claimants, no document relating to the occupation and income of the deceased has been filed by the claimants.

However, looking to the occupation of the deceased on the date of accident, nature of job and minimum wages prevailing on the date of accident, this Court is of the view that Rs.8,000/- would be the appropriate monthly income of the appellant in the present case.

11. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:
Notional income of the claimant is being taken as Rs.8,000/- per month.
By adding 40% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra)

(8000 x 40/100)}.
Out of this amount, 1/4th personal expenditure to be deducted, as there are six claimants.

Now actual monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.8,400/- {11200  (11200 x 1/4)}.
Actual yearly income of the deceased comes to Rs.1,00,800/- (8400 x 12)
Deceased was aged about 28 years at the time of accident and the accident is of the year 2017,

therefore, in view of Smt Sarla Verma (supra), multiplier of 17 would be applicable to calculate the total loss of dependency, which comes to Rs.17,13,600/- (100800 x 17).
Mac 62 of 2021 Rs.40,000/- each to the claimants towards Spousal, Filial, and Parental consortium, Funeral expenses-15,000/-, Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/- in view of the case of Nanu Ram (supra), and 10% enhancement of the same in every three years

Now total compensation comes to Rs.20,37,600/- (1713600 + 324000)
12.
For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.8,86,000/- already awarded by the Tribunal is now enhanced to Rs.20,37,600/-.
Thereby, the claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.11,51,600/- (2037600  886000).
the additional amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.

On such deposit by the Insurance Company,
Rs.8,00,000/- shall be deposited (two lakhs each) in name of appellants-2, 3, 4 and 5 for the respective period of their attaining majority in Fixed Deposit at any Nationalized Bank.
Remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants through Bank transaction/Account payee cheque in terms and proportion mentioned in Para-12 of the impugned award dated 26.07.2019.
14. Appeal is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above.
15. No order as to costs.
